London, 8<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**Platinum** gained for a sixth day on speculation that plans to bolster the U.S. economy will support metal demand. It jumped yesterday above $1,000/oz for the first time in 12 weeks. U.S. President-elect Barack Obama has proposed a $775 billion stimulus. The Treasury has pledged $13.4 billion to help General Motors pay bills and $6 billion for lender GMAC LLC. The metal reached $1,005.50 yesterday, the highest since Oct. 15. Palladium for immediate delivery was down 1.1 % at $194.75 an ounce. _Source:  Bloomberg_ 

**Mazda Motor Corp.** has announced the world’s first market application of single-nanocatalyst technology in automobile catalytic converters. This highly durable new catalyst significantly reduces the amount of precious metals used and effectively purifies vehicle exhaust gases. It will first be introduced in the all-new Mazda3 (Mazda Axela in Japan) which will commence global sales this year.  With the singlenanocatalyst, the underfloor catalytic converter requires only 0.15g/L of precious metals, approximately 70 % less than the 0.55g/L required in the previous model. Along with a substantial reduction in precious metal usage, the Mazda3 continues to qualify as a Super Ultra-Low Emissions Vehicle in Japan by achieving exhaust emissions that are at least 75 % cleaner than the government’s 2005 regulations. Mazda will progressively introduce the single-nanocatalyst to all its global markets. _Source:  JCN Network_ 

**The Chinese auto market** remains a beacon of hope to foreign carmakers battered by shrinking demand in the US and other major markets, despite the slowdown in 2008 sales.   “The Chinese vehicle market will keep growing, though at a slower rate than before, and global automakers have to step up efforts in China to boost sales,” said Yale Zhang, of consultancy CSM Worldwide Corp.  He estimated that China auto sales in 2008 grew 7 % year on year and, with help from the government stimulus package, a further increase of 6 % in 2009 can be expected.  GF Securities also recently predicted that the market descent will hit bottom in Q2, after which demand will revive.  Ford said financial woes will not affect the group’s expansion strategy in China.  It will produce its all-new Fiesta subcompact at its JV in Nanjing from Q1.  GM and its JVs completed several important projects recently, including the expansion of SAICGM-Wuling’s plant in Qingdao and the second phase of its Liuzhou West Plant.  In addition, Shanghai GM invested 2.67 billion yuan to open its second vehicle manufacturing plant in Shenyang late last month, producing the new Chevrolet Cruze, and Audi AG is planning to establish a China branch in Beijing to reinforce local sourcing, and research and development. _Source:  China Daily_ 

**Eskom** affirmed that the demand for 2009 was “very unpredictable” as the depth of the economic downturn was still being assessed and the speed of recove

ry was uncertain.  “A clearer picture will only emerge in February, as industry assesses their order books.  At this stage, a similar demand to 2008 is anticipated”. This anticipated supply demand situation derived from two main factors, firstly, that there has been a decrease in demand because of energy saving measures, but a significant portion was owing to the impact of the economic downturn on mining and industrial customers.  The second factor was that new plants, such as the open-cycle gas-turbines and return-to-service plants in the first half of the year were providing additional megawatts for the overall system.  These factors have reduced the risk of load shedding but it could not be eliminated, and “the power system is still vulnerable”, said Eskom. _Source:  Engineering Weekly_
